history: To visit someone is to go and see them. Latin videre, ‘to see’, produced visere, ‘to look at carefully’, and then the frequent form visitare, ‘to go and see again and again’. Italian visita covers a social visit (una visita a un amico), a tour (visita guidata) and, importantly for residents, a medical appointment: una visita medica, una visita specialistica. The past participle of videre, visto, also became a noun. Il visto is the visa in your passport, the stamp that says the document was ‘seen’ and approved, and English visa came from the same Latin participle through French. When you look for a vista you find the same root again: the view from a window.
historyEinfach: Visita comes from Latin videre, ‘to see’. A visit means ‘to go and see’. In Italian, una visita can be a visit to a friend, a guided tour or a doctor's appointment. The word visto, ‘visa’, comes from the same verb. It means a document that has been ‘seen’ and approved.

chain: Latin visa (charta) ‘a document that was seen’
elsewhere.text: The English visa and the Italian visto both come from the verb videre. In Italian you ask for un visto d'ingresso.
